This paper examines the computational expressiveness of Constraint Handling Rules (CHR) by analyzing the size of atoms within its rules. We demonstrate that the head size serves as a significant indicator of expressive power, as restricting this size enables the derivation of numerous significant results. We provide a characterization of the finite sets of rules where limiting the head size preserves computational expressiveness, as well as an associated decidability theorem. Additionally, we establish a result showing that for any integer $n \geq 2$, a set of $n$-rule rules with bounded head size can be expressively equivalent to a set of $n$-rule rules with unbounded head size.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need to train models with limited labeled data. Although recent advances in Eigen-Reptile have demonstrated superior performance in few-shot classification, the method remains susceptible to sampling bias and label noise. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel approach that integrates sampling strategies with a robust loss function. Specifically, the method employs Eigen-Laplacian Reptile to mitigate sampling bias and utilizes Eigen-Reptile as a base for learning a robust loss function. Furthermore, the approach incorporates a novel sampling strategy that leverages the Eigen-Laplacian metric to select representative prototypes, and introduces a regularization term to suppress the influence of label noise. Experimental results on the miniImageNet and CIFAR-100 datasets confirm that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art FSL methods.

This study introduces a novel framework for predicting Alzheimer's disease cognitive phenotypes by integrating MRI-derived features with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. We trained a deep learning model using a dataset of 1,000 ADNI participants, comprising 500 diagnosed with AD and 500 CN controls. The model's performance was evaluated on a test set of 1,000 participants, consisting of 500 AD cases and 500 CN controls. The results indicate that the proposed method outperforms the baseline, which relies solely on MMSE scores, achieving an accuracy of 78.1% and an AUC of 0.81.

Ethical analysis is fundamental to the development of trustworthy Artificial Intelligence. However, current research indicates that the prevailing ethical frameworks within AI Ethics literature are often applied in ways that are too rigid, overly focused on specific cases, and insufficiently systematic. This study introduces a novel methodology for AI ethical analysis, grounded in the concept of a "systematicity spectrum." This spectrum is defined by the extent to which the analysis is conducted in a structured, systematic, and repeatable manner. By examining the state of the field, the authors demonstrate that existing practices frequently fall short of high levels of systematicity. Furthermore, the paper outlines specific strategies to enhance the systematicity of ethical analysis, thereby fostering greater trust in the deployment of AI technologies.

The concept of a trio of languages was originally introduced by McNaughton and Zimand in 1977 to define a class of languages closed under union, intersection, and star operations. This framework was later broadened by Kari and others in 1990 to encompass boolean combinations of languages, a development that has since been extended to infinite words. In this work, we investigate the properties of these structures specifically over infinite word sequences. Our primary finding establishes that the trio generated by the boolean closure is the only decidable one. Furthermore, we demonstrate that any boolean-closed family of languages closed under concatenation and star operations is undecidable. In this context, we explore the properties of these structures specifically over infinite word sequences. Our main finding establishes that the trio generated by the boolean closure is the only decidable one. Additionally, we demonstrate that any boolean-closed family of languages closed under concatenation and star operations is undecidable.

This paper introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework designed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, combining a low-resolution deep neural network (DNN) with a traditional least squares (LS) method. The proposed scheme utilizes a DNN to forecast channel parameters based on the LS baseline prediction, thereby enhancing accuracy. Specifically, the DNN takes the initial LS output as input and refines it to correct estimation errors. The study evaluates the performance of this hybrid approach against conventional DNN-based and standard LS methods through extensive simulations. The results demonstrate that the hybrid scheme achieves superior performance compared to both standalone alternatives.

Recent discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental results for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$, combined with the global kaon matrix element analysis, suggest physics beyond the Standard Model. This paper examines the implications of such new physics within the framework of a generic $U(1)_{X}$ extension of the Standard Model, which accommodates both lepton and baryon number. We demonstrate that this model can simultaneously resolve the muon $g-2$ anomaly, the muon-to-positron mass ratio $(\mu/e)_{\mu/e}$ discrepancy, and the proton radius anomaly. Furthermore, we show that the model accounts for the observed sterile neutrino signals from the LSND and MINOS experiments, as well as the LSND and MINOS anomalies.

This study introduces a new network architecture for semantic segmentation of infrared images, leveraging dilated convolution layers to capture both local and global context. This context is synthesized through a hierarchical feature pyramid, which is subsequently decoded into segmentation masks. Evaluated on a newly created benchmark dataset for building detection, the model achieved an F1-score of 0.72, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.

Data reuse is a vital component of modern data science, yet it faces significant hurdles due to the presence of private information that must be separated from shared data. This paper introduces a new framework for data reuse that employs a novel data view separation technique. This approach utilizes a data reuse framework to isolate private information, thereby enabling the reutilization of datasets. Unlike previous methods, our technique offers a more comprehensive solution to this challenge. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our data view separation technique through experiments on a dataset containing information about a specific individual. This approach successfully removes private information, ensuring that the resulting data is safe for reuse.

This emission, which peaks at 160 GHz, is primarily concentrated in the galaxy's central region, with a peak intensity of 1.5 mJy/beam. The spectral energy distribution (SED) of this emission is modeled using a modified blackbody with a temperature of 60 K and a dust mass of 1.2 × 10⁷ M☉. The derived dust-to-metallicity ratio is 0.04, which is lower than the value found in the Milky Way. The spatial distribution of the hot dust is compared with radio data from the VLA and ALMA, revealing a strong correlation between radio luminosity and hot dust emission. The hot dust is predominantly found in the galaxy's spiral arms, where it is closely associated with regions of intense radio emission. The SED of the hot dust is also compared with that of the cold dust, showing that the hot dust is more prevalent in the spiral arms and in the galaxy's central regions. Although recent advancements have propelled large language models toward human-level performance on various tasks, these systems often lack the capacity to comprehend human moral reasoning. This study introduces MORALCOT, a novel prompting approach designed to enhance AI moral reasoning through the construction of a narrative chain. By leveraging a pre-trained moral reasoning dataset, we developed a reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) framework to train a model capable of generating a prompt consisting of a moral scenario, associated question, and a moral reasoning narrative. Experimental results demonstrate that this prompt significantly boosts the performance of pre-trained language models on specific moral reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, we conducted a human evaluation of the generated narratives, which revealed that the proposed MORALCOT prompt achieves a higher quality score compared to outputs from the RLHF-trained model alone.

A valuation ring that has a residue field with characteristic $p>0$ serves as the direct limit of discrete valuation rings, which are themselves finite modules over their respective subrings of $p$-bases. Furthermore, when the valuation is nontrivial, one can establish that these rings are not merely finite modules but are actually finite extensions derived from a unique valuation ring that possesses a residue field of characteristic $0$.

The Dirac equation in two dimensions is examined across various scientific domains, ranging from condensed matter physics to high-energy physics. We explore its fundamental solutions alongside the concepts of bound states and scattering within the framework of form factors. Additionally, we analyze the Dirac equation under both scalar and vector potentials, highlighting how these potentials influence the equation's structure.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has proven effective for solving complex, multi-agent cooperative driving applications. By leveraging MPC's ability to anticipate future states, it can effectively manage interactions among multiple vehicles. This study introduces a novel MPC-based longitudinal controller designed for cooperative adaptive cruise control (ACC) systems. The approach employs a receding horizon strategy to determine the optimal longitudinal control for a specific vehicle, accounting for the predicted positions of surrounding vehicles. The objective function is structured to minimize longitudinal control effort while simultaneously reducing deviations from a target longitudinal speed and inter-vehicle spacing. Additionally, to ensure safety, the optimization incorporates constraints that guarantee collision avoidance. The paper further details the mathematical derivation of the optimal control law, its implementation, and the solution to the associated Riccati equation. Finally, extensive numerical simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed controller in various traffic scenarios.

In the digital age, social media serves as a primary source of information, yet its credibility is frequently challenged. This study investigates how users evaluate the reliability of content through peer interactions. We introduce a novel approach that leverages the social graph to determine a document's credibility. Our method integrates two key components: first, a classifier that categorizes user comments as supportive, critical, or neutral; second, a credibility scoring system that calculates the likelihood of a document's authenticity based on the sentiment and connectivity of its associated social graph. To validate this approach, we conducted a large-scale experiment utilizing a dataset of 1.5 million tweets and over 10 million associated comments. The results demonstrate that our method achieves a 10% improvement in accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The integration of 5G and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies has enabled the development of a smart transportation system capable of supporting intelligent transportation applications. This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a framework designed to assist road operators in managing network resources during traffic emergencies. By leveraging a network-wide view, $\pi$-ROAD utilizes a comprehensive view of the network to identify emergency events and automatically manages IoT network resources to facilitate emergency communication. Specifically, $\pi$-ROAD employs a network-wide view to detect emergencies, automatically manages IoT network resources to support emergency communications, and provides operators with a comprehensive view of the network to aid in resource management.

This study presents a simulation-based analysis of a collaborative task involving a mobile manipulator, where the 6-DOF manipulator is mounted on a mobile base. The system's performance is evaluated using the RRTConnect algorithm for motion planning and the Artificial Potential Fields (APF) collision avoidance method. The results indicate that while the APF algorithm successfully prevents collisions, it causes the mobile base to deviate from the planned trajectory.

The trajectory of urban development is increasingly defined by the integration of autonomous systems and machine intelligence. As autonomous vehicles become more prevalent, they are reshaping transportation networks, shifting the spatial organization of cities, and altering the daily routines of residents. This shift is also transforming the operational frameworks of urban management, as autonomous systems increasingly take on roles in decision-making processes. This paper examines the transformative potential of autonomous systems within the built environment, exploring how their widespread adoption will impact urban governance, infrastructure, and social interactions.

This study investigates online caching with side information, where a cache of capacity $k$ receives requests over time. Upon each request, the system receives a side information signal $x$ representing the likelihood that item $i$ is optimal, and the algorithm must decide which stored item to evict. We introduce a novel framework for analyzing this problem, where the adversary reveals the next optimal choice sequentially, and the algorithm must respond immediately by deciding on an eviction. We demonstrate that this approach offers significant flexibility, allowing for the derivation of competitive bounds under various scenarios—including when $x$ is perfectly accurate, when $k$ is infinite, or when the algorithm possesses prior knowledge of the request sequence distribution. Specifically, we prove that the competitive ratio is bounded by $1 + \mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon$ represents the prediction error. Furthermore, we show that the competitive ratio can be reduced to $1 + \mathcal{O}(\epsilon \log(1/k))$ when the cache size approaches infinity. We also establish that the competitive ratio improves to $1 + \mathcal{O}(\epsilon \log k)$ if the request distribution is known beforehand.

We introduce a new Trilateral Attention Network (TrANet) designed for image segmentation, which integrates a multi-scale convolutional neural network with a specialized attention module. This module comprises three distinct paths—each with unique configurations—designed to capture features at varying scales and spatial resolutions. By leveraging the complementary strengths of these paths, the model effectively captures both local and global contextual information. TrANet demonstrates superior performance on both semantic segmentation and instance segmentation tasks, outcompeting current state-of-the-art methods. Notably, it achieves this with fewer parameters and a lower computational cost than competing models.

This paper examines the torsion constraints within the linearized supergeometry of superspace. By applying these constraints to gauge fields residing in superspace, we derive a specific set of differential equations that they must fulfill. Conversely, when this approach is extended to the linearized supermanifold, the corresponding torsion constraints translate into conditions on pullback maps defined on the supermanifold's differential forms.

The efficacy of learning models relies heavily on the quality of their training data. While current evaluation methods typically assess model performance at the aggregate level, we propose a novel approach that evaluates data quality at the individual instance level. This method utilizes a model trained on a dataset to quantify the specific contribution of each training example, thereby identifying which data points exert the most influence on model outcomes. We demonstrate that this approach offers a more granular assessment of data quality than traditional techniques, effectively highlighting the impact of noisy or anomalous data points. Furthermore, we validate the proposed approach through experiments across three distinct datasets.

We examine how non-abelian matrix Berry phases influence charge pumping within the quantum Hall surface. Our analysis reveals that the quantum evolution of the system's ground state drives the quantum quenches necessary for this process. By employing a quantum quench approach, we demonstrate that the non-abelian matrix Berry phase facilitates charge pumping in two distinct ways: initially, it generates a quantum pumping current that scales linearly with the system's size, and second, it introduces a phase offset into the pumping cycle. We further establish that this offset can be regulated by tuning the initial state parameters. Additionally, we find that while the magnitude of the quantum pumping current remains unaffected by disorder, the offset experience significant suppression under strong disorder conditions.

We introduce the METRO language models, a family of T5-based architectures trained across 128 distinct languages using the massively multilingual WMT dataset. These models are trained using a novel approach that combines a highly efficient data preselection strategy with a new pretraining loss function, resulting in state-of-the-art performance on the WMT benchmark while utilizing only 1/16th of the training data and computational resources compared to prior work. Our models, ranging from 600M to 3B parameters, are publicly accessible via the HuggingFace hub. Evaluations on GLUE, SQuAD, and XQK datasets reveal that METRO-LM models match or surpass the capabilities of significantly larger predecessors, delivering superior efficiency and performance.

We introduce a protocol for determining the topology of quantum networks that relies solely on local measurements. This method utilizes the correlations between local observables to identify network links, offering a practical and efficient solution that eliminates the need for global measurements or prior knowledge of the system's state. Furthermore, our approach is adaptable to diverse quantum platforms and remains effective even when local noise is present. We validate this technique through numerical simulations involving various network architectures, demonstrating that it achieves high fidelity with minimal resources.

This research investigates how different introduction strategies influence the ability of visualizations to explain themselves to viewers. We conducted a study comparing three methods: (1) a single, comprehensive explanation covering the entire visualization, (2) a sequential approach where sections are explained in order, and (3) a demand approach allowing users to request explanations for specific parts. Our findings indicate that neither method holds a consistent advantage across all scenarios; however, the demand approach emerges as the most effective strategy overall.

The study of Floquet heating in quantum systems has gained significant attention due to its relevance in controlling many-body systems optically. This work examines Floquet heating within the context of a quantum nonlinear optical amplifier, specifically focusing on how it influences system order. We demonstrate that, under certain conditions, Floquet heating can enhance order, whereas in other scenarios, it diminishes order. These findings offer valuable insights for the optical manipulation of many-body systems and may serve as a foundation for developing quantum amplifiers with tunable gain.

Counterfactual reasoning, which evaluates how past events would have unfolded differently, is a powerful method for generating plans to achieve specific goals. This paper introduces a novel framework for creating counterfactual plans that incorporates uncertainty regarding the underlying model parameters. We demonstrate that accounting for this uncertainty is crucial for producing more reliable counterfactual strategies. To address this, we present a method for calculating the likelihood of goal satisfaction within a counterfactual plan by integrating uncertainty about the model. Additionally, we introduce a new planning algorithm designed to generate strategies that maximize the probability of success under these uncertain conditions. Our experiments show that plans developed using this approach are more robust against uncertainty compared to those ignoring it.

This paper presents the Cain compiler, a tool that translates SC5 constraints into C code. While other compilers generate similar C outputs, Cain's versions are notably shorter and more readable. The resulting C code exhibits a more structured approach, with distinct functions that map directly to individual constraints.

This study examines the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, emphasizing its influence on the charged states' mass spectrum. We analyze how the generalized Witten effect, manifested through the coupling of gauge fields to global currents, restricts possible spectra for charged states in quantum gravity. This phenomenon also arises from the interaction between gauge fields and global currents, serving as a constraint on the charged states' mass spectrum in quantum gravity. We explore this effect specifically in the context of the AdS$_2$/CFT$_1$ duality.

This study introduces a novel modal logic grounded in possible states-of-affairs, which expands upon the system presented in our prior work. We leverage this framework to develop a sound and complete axiomatic characterization of Aristotle's modal syllogistic from the *Prior Analytics* (A1-9), interpreting these syllogisms through the lens of potential truth-values for propositions and their respective contraries.

We introduce a family of classical causal inequalities designed to verify the non-classical nature of physical processes. These are derived from the violation of the no-signaling principle by the underlying probability distributions, meaning they are violated exclusively by quantum (or non-classical) causal models. Violating these inequalities requires a lower level of detection efficiency compared to traditional Bell inequalities. While classical models cannot violate them, quantum models can do so using either non-local resources or non-classential causal structures. Additionally, a specific instance of these causal inequalities can be breached using only local quantum operations on individual subsystems, a feat that requires a different detection efficiency threshold than that needed for standard Bell inequality violations.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage video encoding, balancing rate constraints and distortion. By employing two distinct critics to evaluate the actions of an actor, the framework learns to minimize distortion while adhering to bit-rate budgets. The first critic, a binary critic, assesses whether a proposed encoding action complies with a specific target rate, outputting a binary result. The second critic, a real-valued critic, evaluates the distortion of the encoded video given the same action. The actor is trained using a reward function that minimizes distortion under compliant conditions but penalizes non-compliant actions heavily. Experiments conducted on the HEVC test sequences demonstrate that this approach surpasses standard reinforcement learning methods in managing rate-distortion optimization and achieves higher PSNR values than the HEVC Test Model (HTM) 2.0 encoder.

This study investigates the gas-phase chemistry of carbon and oxygen within protoplanetary disks, specifically examining how the photo-ablation of carbon-rich grains influences the abundance of carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO$_2$). We developed a comprehensive chemical model that integrates gas-phase reactions with both gas-grain and gas-ablation interactions. Our findings indicate that gas-grain and ablation processes are critical for sustaining a long-lived equilibrium cycle between CO and CO$_2$. Specifically, the formation of CO$_2$ is primarily driven by the reaction between CO and O on grain surfaces, whereas the destruction of CO$_2$ occurs mainly through reactions with H and O$_2$ in the gas phase. Furthermore, we observed that the abundance of CO$_2$ is significantly enhanced in the disk's surface layers due to the photo-ablation of grains.

This study introduces NeuralCut, a framework designed to select cuts for mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) by leveraging deep learning. Unlike existing methods that rely on specific heuristics, NeuralCap utilizes a custom neural network to identify cuts, offering a general approach to this task. Our experiments demonstrate that NeuralCap consistently surpasses current state-of-the-art baselines in selection quality and significantly expands the solver's ability to handle more complex problems.

Duplicate bug reports are a prevalent and costly issue within software development. While traditional methods rely on simple keyword matching to identify exact duplicates, this approach often fails to capture subtle semantic differences between reports. To address this, we introduce a novel NLP-driven approach that combines a pre-trained transformer model with a retrieval mechanism to detect identical bug reports. Our method involves embedding the text of each bug report using the model and calculating the cosine similarity between these vectors to determine duplicates. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in retrieving exact duplicates.

We introduce an effective field theory that captures the essential characteristics of the phase transition occurring in graphene subjected to intense electromagnetic fields. This framework employs a fermion determinant expressed through a Schwinger proper-time analysis, incorporating a perturbative expansion in the fine-structure constant. The resulting effective action is formulated as a four-dimensional functional integral over bosonic fields, explicitly accounting for the non-abelian anomaly. To address the strong-coupling regime, we apply a strongly coupled effective field theory, utilizing a Gaussian approximation for the gauge field alongside a saddle-point evaluation of fermionic modes. This approach yields a strongly coupled effective theory with a non-trivial potential for the electromagnetic field, indicating a first-order phase transition. Finally, we examine the implications of this framework for the quantum electrodynamics of strong fields, specifically focusing on the phase transition of the vacuum within the Euler-Heisenberg model.

This paper introduces a self-teacher-student framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) by integrating two components: a standard BiLSTM-CRF architecture and a transformer-based teacher model. The teacher model is trained on a dataset expanded by the teacher itself, while the student model learns from the teacher's predictions. Experiments conducted on the OntoNotes 5.0 corpus demonstrate that this framework significantly improves NER performance.

The travel and hospitality sector is a massive global industry that has seen significant growth over the past decade. With the rise of social media, travelers and experts can now share real-time travel experiences, effectively creating a vast repository of tourism-related information. This study examines the insights gained from analyzing social media data to uncover patterns that can aid destination marketing and management. We introduce a novel method for extracting and visualizing data regarding attractions and activities based on Twitter posts. Our analysis of posts containing location tags reveals that Las Vegas is the most prominent destination, while "dining" represents the most common activity type. Furthermore, we developed a new metric to quantify the popularity of specific attractions and activities within any given location. This metric is designed to be easily adaptable for future research. Ultimately, this research demonstrates how leveraging social media data can uncover valuable insights that empower businesses to make more informed decisions.

This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to forecast the effective properties of microstructured materials. The model predicts homogenized elastic tensors for two-phase composites, varying across different volume fractions and geometric patterns. The training dataset was generated using the asymptotic homogenization method, which is a rigorous analytical technique for estimating effective properties. The proposed architecture utilizes a deep neural network with a multi-input configuration to process both volume fraction and geometric data. The findings demonstrate that this method achieves high accuracy in modeling two-phase elastic homogenization. Furthermore, the model exhibits robust generalization capabilities, successfully handling unseen geometric patterns and volume fractions during inference.

The GPI observations, conducted in the I-band at 1.65 microns, were taken in 2016 and 2017, while the star's primary companion was observed in 2018 using the SPHERE instrument on the Very Large Telescope. The companion was not detected in the SPHERE data, likely due to the instrument's limited inner working angle. However, the non-detection in the SPHERE dataset is consistent with the earlier detection by GPI, assuming the companion's brightness follows a spectral energy distribution typical of young stellar objects. This study examines the correspondence between finite-length geodesics on a sphere and zero-energy trajectories in a specific potential, as well as the relationship between finite-energy free-motion paths on a sphere and finite-energy orbits in that same potential. These connections are established through the algebraic structure of the sphere's conformal group. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the conformal group's action on a sphere can be realized as the action of an associated $d$-dimensional conformally invariant potential system on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

This paper examines the existence of non-trivial solutions for non-local integro-differential equations featuring a parameter, utilizing a combination of topological degree theory and nonlinear potential theory.

This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-object filtering that utilizes unlabeled data. By integrating the generalized Poisson multi-Bernoulli filter with a Gibbs sampler, our proposed solution addresses a critical limitation of conventional generalized Poisson-based methods: the inability to trace trajectories beyond the current time step. This new framework significantly enhances trajectory estimation capabilities while maintaining the computational efficiency characteristic of standard single-pass generalized Poisson filters.

The paper introduces a novel stability assessment criterion for large-scale power systems with high-penetration of power converters, based on the concept of stability margins. Unlike traditional approaches, this method avoids the need to calculate equilibrium points or linearized models, thereby eliminating potential errors stemming from their misapplication. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this criterion through a case study utilizing a 39-bus system equipped with a Voltage Source Converter (VSC).

This study introduces a novel approach to signature verification that incorporates forgery detection, utilizing a single genuine signature. The framework employs a two-stage process: first, a signature template is generated from the single authentic sample, and second, a deep neural network (DNN) is trained to verify identities and detect forgeries using that template. The template generation phase extracts features based on three dimensions: distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability. Distinctiveness is addressed through a local feature detector and descriptor; complexity is modeled via a Markov model; and repeatability is represented by a graph-based structure. The model's performance is evaluated on the CASIA and MC-CST forgeries-detection datasets, with results indicating that explicitly modeling these three factors significantly enhances the system's ability to detect forgeries.

This work establishes that Hardy sums can be understood as oriented geodesics in the Farey space, specifically within the boundary of the unit tangent bundle to the upper half-plane under the action of the modular group. We further demonstrate that these geodesics can be naturally extended into the extended real line, $\mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$, as oriented paths. This paper presents a novel framework that synergizes ML and QC to enhance sampling of rare conformational transitions. We introduce a quantum-inspired algorithm that leverages the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to calculate electronic energies and forces for small molecules. By utilizing quantum-inspired techniques to accelerate ML model training, we demonstrate that this approach significantly improves sampling efficiency for rare events. Furthermore, we show that the proposed method is highly adaptable to hybrid ML-QC paradigms, such as those employing density functional theory (DFT).

The MAPPIES code, a novel Monte-Carlo tool designed for polarimetry, simulates the polarization characteristics of X-ray and gamma-ray photons as they traverse various optical instruments. It is built upon the established GEANT4 framework, utilizing its extensive database of particle interactions to model photon behavior. This simulation accounts for the specific physical processes governing photon polarization, including linear polarization from Compton scattering and circular polarization arising from pair production. The code's efficacy is demonstrated through its application to the POLGAMMA telescope, a ground-based instrument intended for polarimetry. Furthermore, the tool's versatility is highlighted by its application to the Fermi LAT, a space-based detector.

This study examines how the seasonal development of sea-ice thickness categories evolves in the presence of open water, utilizing a framework based on the stochastic advection-diffusion equation. The analysis focuses on the stochastic dynamics of the category probability function (CPF) and the category probability flux (CPF). By employing a stochastic approach, the model incorporates both deterministic and stochastic diffusion terms to capture the variability in ice thickness. The results indicate that open water significantly alters the seasonal CPF dynamics, leading to a reduction in the mean maximum thickness and an increase in the category with the highest probability. Additionally, the study investigates the role of stochastic diffusion in shaping these seasonal CPF dynamics.

We present two families of degree-$n$ Hermitian curve-based covers, denoted as $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ and $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$. The first family is characterized by being totally ramified at every point, whereas the second family exhibits total ramification at precisely $n+1$ distinct points. We establish that $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ constitutes a bi-elliptic curve whenever $s$ is an even integer, whereas $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$ is bi-elliptic if and only if $s$ is an odd integer. Furthermore, we demonstrate that $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ is a bi-Heyman curve whenever $s$ is an even integer, while $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$ is bi-Heyman if and only if $s$ is an odd integer.

Singing voice synthesis has seen significant advancements in recent years, yet challenges persist in bridging the gap between academic research and commercial deployment. This paper presents a novel singing voice synthesis framework that integrates a singing-specific vocoder with a singing-specific autoencoder. The autoencoder is trained to reconstruct the mel-spectrogram from a single input, effectively capturing the underlying singing characteristics. This learned representation is then used to guide the vocoder in generating high-quality audio waveforms. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces NIPS4Bplus, an advanced version of the NIPS4B deep learning model designed for bird population monitoring and ecoacoustic surveillance. By integrating a novel dataset of bird calls, NIPS4Bplus demonstrates enhanced performance in detecting bird species within audio recordings. The model, which utilizes a U-Net architecture, was trained on a curated collection of 1,000 recordings from the Australian Wetlands Trust, featuring calls from 12 bird species. Evaluation on a test set of 1,000 recordings from the Australian Wetlands Trust revealed that NIPS-Bplus achieved an F1-score of 0.94, surpassing the original NIPS4B's score of 0.91. This improvement stems from the incorporation of the newly acquired dataset. The research also examined the model's ability to localize bird calls within audio files, highlighting its potential for use in ecoacoustic research and monitoring bird populations.

We introduce a unified, model-based framework for jointly calibrating event and frame-based sensors. This approach enables extrinsic calibration between frame-based sensors and event cameras, as well as the alignment of multiple event cameras. The framework utilizes a novel event-based pose graph optimization method that incorporates novel pose priors derived from frame-based sensors. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves high accuracy and robustness, with performance comparable to that of frame-based cameras.

Graph learning has proven effective in numerous domains, including social networking, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological and medical applications. However, existing research predominantly relies on graph data where node features are known. This paper introduces a new learning framework designed for graph data with missing features, a scenario that is both common and underexplored in current literature. We introduce a graph autoencoder that integrates both node features and graph structures, utilizing a graph convolutional network to capture structural information and an autoencoder to recover node features. Furthermore, we develop a new loss function to jointly optimize the graph convolutional network and the autoencoder, thereby learning robust node embeddings. Experimental results on real-world graph datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

This work analyzes exceptional collections within the homological projective duality framework for the degree-2 Hirzebruch surface, demonstrating that the braid group acting on four strands acts transitively on the set of such collections.

This study introduces a novel augmented reality (AR) system designed to assist in retinal surgery. The approach utilizes a camera to capture the patient's retina, which is then reconstructed into a three-dimensional (3D) model. A spotlight projection mechanism is employed to guide the 3D surgical process, while the system simultaneously provides real-time two-dimensional (2D) visual feedback of the retinal surface. This dual-modality feedback—combating the limitations of projection through an explicit 2D overlay—offers a more intuitive and precise navigation aid for surgeons. To validate the system's effectiveness, a series of experiments were conducted, demonstrating the method's superior performance in terms of accuracy and reliability.

We express the $F$-polynomial associated with a cluster variable in a cluster algebra as a product of $F$-polynomials belonging to seeds containing rank-one clusters. This product formula yields a new representation as a sum of cluster monomials. Consequently, we deduce a combinatorial expression for the $F$-polynomials of acyclic cluster algebras, which expands upon the established formula by Chekoni, Fomin, and Zelevinsky. Our approach relies on the methodology introduced by Lee and Zelevinsky.

The FIDO2 standard, which is gaining significant traction, is driving the world toward passwordless authentication. This approach aims to enhance user experience by reducing the frequency of password resets and to mitigate security risks associated with passwords. However, the FIDO2 framework relies on a client-side authenticator that is not yet supported by standard web browsers, necessitating a browser extension to enable its use. This paper details the architecture and design of the FIDO2 browser extension, which facilitates passwordless login for web applications. We also present a preliminary study evaluating the effectiveness of the extension in promoting widespread adoption of FIDO2-based passwordless authentication.

Although the Weyl-Wigner formalism has been extended to multi-qubit systems, it fails to encompass fundamental quantum phenomena involving individual qubits. This shortcoming stems from its inability to represent quantum states as a collection of classical bits. Consequently, this work introduces a revised Weyl-Wigner framework that utilizes the Bloch sphere to model single qubits. By applying this approach, we derive a star product for qubits and investigate its algebraic characteristics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this star product can be expressed through a deformation of a standard product of matrix-valued functions, and we examine the associated deformation parameters.

This paper introduces a user study examining how interface design in video applications influences users' perceived sense of control. We recruited 20 participants to complete a series of tasks using five different apps, with a focus on the playback controls. Our results indicate that while some interfaces successfully enhanced feelings of control, others diminished them. We attribute these differences to specific interface elements, such as the presence of a progress bar, and the ability to adjust playback speed.

This paper examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus when compared to reactive TTM machines. We demonstrate that every reactive TM can be faithfully translated into the $\pi$-calculus, and conversely, every reactive TTM can be compiled into a reactive TTM from a $\pi$-calculus. These results indicate that both formalisms are capable of specifying behaviors that cannot be executed in finite time. Furthermore, we prove that $\pi$-calculus offers a more succinct representation for such behaviors compared to reactive TTM machines.

This study introduces a distinct type of Gray code for ordered trees, structured so that consecutive codes correspond to ordered trees that differ only by a single parent-child relationship. The sequence is organized such that adjacent entries switch from one specific tree to another by moving a child node to its parent.

Reconstructing particle trajectories in heavy ion collisions is complicated by the high density of overlapping paths. This study introduces a new algorithm designed to trace these paths through the entire ALICE Time Projection Chamber (TPC) using its wire chamber data. The method employs a deep learning approach, where a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is trained on simulated events to identify tracks. The CNN is fed with wire chamber data derived from a specific starting point, where wires are arranged in a grid. The model's output is a probability map indicating the likelihood of a track passing through each cell. By applying a greedy traceback technique, the trajectory is reconstructed by sequentially selecting cells with the highest probabilities. The performance of this method is evaluated using simulated events and compared against the standard ALICE track finding algorithm.

This study introduces a novel time-discontinuous prismatic space-time finite-element approach for simulating free-surface flows. By extending the well-established discontinuous Galerkin (DG) framework to three dimensions, the method offers distinct advantages over prior time-continuous prism schemes. Specifically, the ability to resolve flow features at the local spatial and temporal resolution allows for the accurate modeling of sharp discontinuities, such as breaking waves and hydraulic jumps, without the need for ad hoc limiting techniques. Furthermore, the free-surface boundary conditions are handled via a Lagrangian formulation, which effectively mitigates the numerical errors associated with artificial surface diffusion.

A circular $r_{_k}$-flow in a signed graph $G$ is defined as an orientation of $G$ paired with a labeling of vertices using integers modulo $p$ such that the sum of edge labels around every cycle is congruent to zero modulo $k$. The study establishes that a signed graph admits a circular $r_{_k}$-flow if and only if it possesses a mod $k$-orientation, thereby confirming that these two concepts are mathematically equivalent. Furthermore, the work derives various corollaries and explores connections with the concept of mod $k$-biflows.

We present a deterministic approach for the Modular Subset Sum problem that achieves a running time of $O(n+L)$, where $L$ represents the largest number in the input. This represents an improvement over the prior best algorithm by Balasubramaniam et al., which operated in $O(l\log l)$ time.

The study investigates the influence of LanB1 and SCAR mutants on hemocyte motility and the formation of actin-rich membrane protrusions, such as lamellipodia and filopodia, using a 3D collagen gel assay. In this setup, hemocytes were seeded onto collagen gels containing either a control, LanB1, or SCAR mutant. Time-lapse imaging was employed to track cell movement, while immunostaining was performed to visualize actin and microtubule structures. Results indicate that cells seeded on gels with either the LanB1 or SCAR mutant exhibited reduced motility compared to control cells. Furthermore, cells exposed to mutant conditions displayed fewer actin-rich protrusions, suggesting a diminished capacity for migration. These findings demonstrate that both LanB1 and SCAR mutations significantly impair hemocyte migration within a 3D collagen gel environment.

This study introduces c-siam, a novel speech-language pre-training architecture designed to enhance the extraction of linguistic information from audio data. By utilizing a contrastive learning framework, c-siam aligns the acoustic representations of a word with its textual form, effectively overcoming the limitations of prior models that relied solely on word-pair similarity. We further developed a graph-based data augmentation strategy to boost model performance and validated c-siam across three distinct downstream tasks: automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-sentence translation (ST), and zero-shot speaker verification (SV). Our experimental results demonstrate that c-siam significantly improves ASR and ST outcomes across various test sets, while also achieving substantial gains in SV performance.

This study introduces a refined version of the neutrino-nucleon parton distribution function (PDF) framework, which is built upon the global analysis of the CTEQ15 collaboration. The new model, CTEQ15NE, incorporates recent LHC data on W boson production and incorporates the latest measurements of neutrino-nucleon total and differential cross sections. This update yields significantly improved agreement with experimental data regarding neutrino-nucleon total and differential cross sections, as well as W boson production. The analysis further demonstrates that the updated CTEQ15NE model provides a superior fit to the neutrino-nucleon total and differential cross section measurements compared to the previous CTEQ15-based PDFs. Additionally, the study reports the first-ever measurement of the neutrino-nucleon total cross section at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 8.16$ TeV, which is consistent with previous results within uncertainties. The new PDFs are also found to be consistent with the CTEQ15-based PDFs, which is a significant result given the large uncertainties in the neutrino-nucleon total and differential cross section measurements. The analysis also reports the first-ever measurement of the neutrino-nucleon total cross section at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 8.16$ TeV, which is consistent with previous results within uncertainties. This study addresses the stabilization of linear systems influenced by linearly coupled hidden Markov chains. We propose a separation-based model-free adaptive control scheme that merges a data-driven estimator with a deterministic controller. The algorithm achieves almost sure system stabilization by combining stochastic stability from the estimator with stability ensured by the deterministic component. To evaluate the performance of this approach, we compare it against a model-based method that relies on known Markov chain transition probabilities. We demonstrate that, under specific mild conditions, both the proposed model-free and the optimal model-based control strategies yield identical performance.

This paper introduces BTAI, a novel Behavior Tree Abstraction method designed to enhance the efficiency of learning abstractions for Behavior Trees (BTs). BTAI surpasses existing solutions by achieving faster task completion times, higher success rates, and reduced memory usage. The BTAI methodology is grounded in a new graph-based metric that quantifies the interconnection between nodes within a BT. Additionally, we evaluate BTAI against two baseline approaches: the established BTA method and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) tailored for learning abstractions for BTs. Experimental results demonstrate that BTAI outperforms BTA in terms of both success rate and execution time, while it surpasses DQN in success rate and computational efficiency.
This study derives the Korteweg-de Vries equation applicable to the surface of a quark gluon plasma, utilizing a specific equation of state for the medium.

This work demonstrates that a compact space's function space (comprising continuous real-valued functions) possesses the linearly Eberlein-Grothendieck property if and only if its Stone-\vC{c}ech compactification is a linear Eberlein space. Additionally, we prove that the linearity of this function space is equivalent to the condition that the product of any two copies remains a K-space.

This study examines the link between the Taylor coefficients of a Hamiltonian function and its specific homological properties tied to isochronicity. Leveraging this relationship, the authors investigate multiple properties of Dulac's vector field to demonstrate that no Hamiltonian polynomial vector field of degree greater than four can exhibit globally uniform periodic orbits.

This study examines the classification of periodic orbits in the Lorenz system, a well-known chaotic system. We categorize these orbits into two groups based on their period lengths: those with periods of 3 or less and those with longer periods. For the latter, we demonstrate that their structure is more intricate, with their topological forms being shaped by orbits possessing shorter periods. Furthermore, we offer a method to calculate the topological zeta function for the periodic orbits of the Lorenz system, utilizing the counts of orbits within specific period ranges.

This study examines the application of Malliavin calculus within statistical models of the exponential family type. We introduce a novel formula for calculating the log-likelihood derivative under the $L^2$ norm of a Hilbert space defined by the model's probability measure. Leveraging this formula alongside integration-by-parts identities, we derive representations for the Hellinger divergence between adjacent probability densities. These derived formulas are subsequently utilized to establish an upper bound on the Hellinger derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the data.

This study examines the spectrum of Laplacians on Riemann surfaces subjected to Teichmüller deformations, specifically within the context of unitary group representations. We demonstrate that the critical exponents associated with these representations are linked to the spectrum of the Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish a variant of Wey's law, proving that the count of representations possessing a critical exponent below a given threshold grows proportionally to a specified power of that exponent.

Fourier transforms are widely used in time-series prediction tasks, yet they are often neglected in deep learning contexts because they are perceived as lacking flexibility. This paper introduces the Autoregressive Fourier Transform (ARFT), a method that enhances traditional autoregressive filtering by incorporating frequency information. By applying a low-pass filter to the autoregressive component, ARFT preserves the interpretability of time shifts while boosting predictive performance. Empirical results indicate that ARFT consistently outperforms standard autoregressive filters across various tasks, including speech recognition, and can be integrated into existing models with minimal effort.

This study examines the compatibility of cosmological models with observational data by analyzing the evolution of energy density and the equation of state. We categorize these models into two groups: those that align with current observations and those that fail to do so. Our analysis reveals that viable models generally feature a positive equation of state and energy density values near zero.

Multi-access edge computing (MEC) has emerged as a promising solution to address the escalating demands of latency-sensitive applications. This study introduces a novel resource allocation framework for Function Service Chaining (FSC) within the MEC environment, aiming to minimize total service costs while adhering to constraints regarding service latency and resource availability. The proposed optimization model is a mixed-integer non-linear program (MINLP) that is decomposed into two distinct subproblems: the server selection problem and the resource allocation problem. The first subproblem is addressed using a greedy algorithm, while the second is solved via a dual decomposition approach. Furthermore, a comprehensive algorithm is developed to integrate these two solutions into a unified, efficient framework. Extensive simulations demonstrate that this proposed method significantly outperforms existing benchmark algorithms in terms of service costs.

We investigate the renormalization group (RG) flow of a two-dimensional Dirac fermion system with a mass term, incorporating a quartic interaction and subject to disorder. Our analysis reveals that the disorder strength, $R$, and the mass, $m$, are mutually coupled. We identify a non-Gaussian fixed point that remains stable across all regimes of $R$; however, its influence is restricted to a finite region within the $(m, R)$ parameter space. In contrast, the Gaussian fixed point exhibits stability in the remaining parameter space. These findings are corroborated by RG calculations performed up to fourth order in the loop expansion.

This study examines the online social behavior of individuals diagnosed with depression compared to a control group. By analyzing user data from the social networking platform Twitter, we investigate how positive life events influence the social networks of depressed users. Our findings indicate that depressed users exhibit greater sensitivity to positive events than control users. Furthermore, we observe that depressed users are more likely to respond to such events by initiating conversations with new connections, a trend that holds true across various types of positive life occurrences.

We investigate the connection between a QCD-like theory and a confocal theory of dark matter, which manifests as a dark sector QCD-like system. This setup offers a natural explanation for the observed mass of the proton within the visible sector, suggesting a similar mass scale for dark protons. Furthermore, this framework provides a mechanism for nucleon-nucleus scattering involving dark matter, which could be detected by existing experiments.

The magnetic behavior of the spin-1/2 square-lattice antiferromagnet Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$ is examined through neutron diffraction and magnetic susceptibility data. This study demonstrates that crystalline electric field effects reduce the Ni$^{2+}$ spin moment to approximately 0.55(2) $\mu_B$, a reduction from the expected value of 1.73(1) $\mu_B$ for a free ion. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the Ni magnetic moments are significantly suppressed along the c-axis, indicating that Ni magnetic correlations are primarily one-dimensional.

In large-scale distributed systems like the Internet of Things, trust is vital for decision-making. However, the sheer volume of data generated by these devices creates a bottleneck for traditional centralized systems, which struggle to process information quickly enough. To address this, we introduce a new framework for distributed trust management that leverages the computational power of edge devices. This framework utilizes a hierarchical approach to manage trust relationships, allowing trust assessments to be cached locally at the edge. This strategy significantly reduces the communication overhead associated with querying remote devices, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of the system.

Although cubic splines are renowned for their smoothness, they fail to maintain data monotonicity, a shortcoming that restricts their utility in specific fields. This paper introduces a technique for generating shape-preserving cubic splines that honor the monotonicity of the original dataset. By applying this method to real-world datasets, we demonstrate its efficacy.

This study examines the evolution of static, spherically symmetric exact black bounces featuring a regular core with minimal rotation. We analyze how these solutions transition between de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometries, as well as the limits where the cosmological constant vanishes. Our results indicate that de Sitter and anti-de Sitter configurations evolve into one another through a series of steps, whereas the case with a null cosmological constant proceeds in a direct transition.

This paper details the Human Annotation Challenge of the 2021 TAC Acoustics, Focal Points Working Group. The initiative involved manually labeling a diverse collection of audio files using time-structured annotations. Although the goal was to annotate over 100 hours of data, the process yielded a limited number of submissions from participants. This document examines the reasons behind the low participation, presents an analysis of the received submissions, and offers guidance for future annotators.

This study examines the evolution of a network following the deletion of a single node, utilizing the largest connected component as a measure of the resulting fragmentation. By analyzing the relationship between avalanche size and the identity of the deleted node, we demonstrate that this relationship exhibits a power-law distribution. This finding indicates that the probability of the largest component's size following node removal follows a power-law distribution.

While discourse-level understanding is crucial for human communication, constructing holistic models for this task remains difficult because it necessitates modeling the entire text. This study introduces a neural architecture designed to capture the full context of long documents by integrating a hierarchical encoder-decoder framework with a novel pointer-copy attention mechanism. This approach enables the model to generate summaries that closely mirror the wording of the original text. We assessed the model's performance across two datasets: the Xsum news summary corpus and a custom collection of scientific abstracts. Empirical results indicate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in discourse summarization.

This paper details the creation of a PML implementation designed for semidiscrete second-order semilagrangian pseudo-spectral schemes. The method is tailored for solving the wave equation in acoustics and elastic wave propagation. The study evaluates the PML's efficacy in both one and three dimensions, analyzing its performance across various spectral configurations. The results demonstrate that, in three-dimensional scenarios, this approach can reduce computational costs by up to 60%.

The study of droplet interactions, a critical component of multiphase flows, has been significantly advanced by the development of the Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) method. This research presents a novel, three-dimensional DNS framework for simulating droplet dynamics, which integrates a level-set approach for interface tracking with a finite-volume method for solving the Navier-Stokes equations. This hybrid technique is designed to accurately capture the complex fluid mechanics occurring within droplet clusters. The proposed model was validated through a series of three-dimensional breakup and collision experiments. The results demonstrate that this new framework can reproduce various breakup modes, including the previously identified "butterfly" type, which had not been observed in earlier three-dimensional studies. Additionally, the paper introduces a novel mechanism of breakup known as "spherical cap breakup." Finally, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of the flow characteristics associated with droplet interactions, focusing on the vorticity and velocity fields.

The proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has driven a surge in traffic demands, necessitating traffic management strategies that are both efficient and scalable. This paper introduces a novel Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-based framework designed to optimize IoT traffic handling. By leveraging the agility of SDN, the proposed method offers a centralized approach to traffic management that adapts to diverse IoT device requirements. The control plane utilizes a machine learning model to forecast traffic patterns, enabling the development of a proactive forwarding strategy. This strategy aims to minimize network congestion and reduce packet loss by anticipating traffic flows before they occur. The study evaluates the proposed framework against traditional routing protocols and other machine learning-based solutions. The results demonstrate that the new method outperforms traditional routing by 15.2% in terms of packet delivery ratio and achieves a 20.5% improvement in reducing packet drops compared to ML-driven dynamic routing.

We present a comprehensive study of the hydrodynamical evolution of a protoplanetary disk surrounding a 1 solar mass star and a 1 Jupiter-mass planet on a highly elliptical orbit. Our simulations reveal that the planet's eccentric orbit significantly alters the disk's architecture, creating a complex, time-varying gap that fluctuates in width and depth throughout the planet's orbital cycle. Furthermore, the disk's midplane temperature and density distributions exhibit substantial variations along the gap's edges, with these changes being more pronounced at the inner gap boundary than at the outer one. These findings suggest that the planet's eccentricity plays a crucial role in shaping the disk's morphology and that the resulting gap structure is likely to evolve over time.

This study examines the application of embedding techniques within the frameworks of Euclidean space, hyperbolic space, and spaces defined by symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices. While SPD-space based models have recently demonstrated success in practical scenarios, the authors provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of the performance bounds for hyperbolic and SPD-space models relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Specifically, the paper establishes that the performance of these alternative models is upper-bounded by a factor of $\sqrt{2}$ relative to Euclidean space models. Furthermore, it is proven that SPD-space models achieve a tighter performance bound than hyperbolic models. These theoretical findings are corroborated through numerical experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This study evaluates the viability of converting natural gas pipelines into transport infrastructure for hydrogen. We model the U.S. pipeline network using a graph where nodes represent interconnection points and edges denote the pipelines themselves. By applying a heuristic algorithm to this model, we determine the minimum number of new links required to connect hydrogen sources to sink locations. Our results indicate that a substantial portion of the necessary network can leverage the existing natural gas infrastructure. Specifically, we find that 80% of the hydrogen network backbone can be repurposed from natural gas lines, with only 20% requiring new construction. This finding suggests that the existing natural gas grid is highly suitable for adaptation to carry low-carbon fuels like hydrogen.

This study introduces a new technique for determining the surface magnetic field (BMF) of a Sun-like star by analyzing the circular polarization spectrum of its photospheric lines. The approach involves modeling the observed line profiles using a two-component model that accounts for both the surface and subsurface magnetic fields. The method was tested on the M-dwarf star GJ 115, which exhibits a magnetic field strength of approximately 1.5 kG. The results indicate that the azimuths of the subsurface and surface magnetic fields are nearly identical, with a difference of less than 10 degrees. Furthermore, the derived subsurface BMF is roughly half the magnitude of the surface BMF, with an estimated depth of 1000 km. The study also examines the implications of these findings for the Sun's magnetic field structure and discusses the potential of this method for future applications.

We introduce a new framework for integrated photonics that leverages topological phases to produce squeezed light. This approach utilizes a nonlinear dimer of photonic quantum spin Hall insulators, where the spin Hall effect facilitates the generation of two-mode squeezed states. Our analysis demonstrates that squeezing efficiency is governed by a topological phase parameter, enabling the production of high-quality vacuum-closed mode squeezing. Furthermore, the proposed system offers a pathway to generate squeezed light at terahertz frequencies, a regime previously inaccessible with existing on-chip technologies.

This paper introduces a trajectory planning approach for drones that integrates a genetic algorithm with a modified particle swarm optimization method. The study evaluates the efficacy of this proposed technique against standard polynomial trajectory methods. Simulation outcomes indicate that the new strategy surpasses polynomial methods in optimizing for minimal travel time.

This paper examines the transition of high-energy physics (HEP) physicists entering the workforce, with a specific focus on the pathways linking to High Energy Physics careers. It details how engaging with former students can facilitate their move from studying physics to securing roles in industry.

The relationship between W boson polarization and the angular distribution of a specific jet relative to the top quark's decay b-quark is examined. This angular variable is defined as the angle between b-quarks originating from the top quark and a specific W boson decay product. It is demonstrated that this observable effectively distinguishes between W bosons produced via the direct and indirect mechanisms. Furthermore, this approach is utilized to investigate the W boson polarization arising from the t → Wb decay.

We derive new sum rules for the $\xi$-moments of the leading-twist D-meson distribution amplitudes (DAs) by employing the corresponding leading-twist wave functions. These new sum rules offer an additional constraint for parameterizing the D-meson DA, thereby enhancing the precision of calculations involving exclusive D-meson processes.

The spectral characteristics of power graphs are a significant area of research, with the eigenvalues of these structures playing a crucial role in analyzing graph invariants. This paper establishes a novel relationship linking the eigenvalues of a power graph to those of its signed subsets, a finding that rectifies prior literature by offering a more comprehensive formula. Building on this relationship, we derive the spectrum for several families of binary power graphs, including those with odd exponents. Furthermore, we examine how these eigenvalues behave asymptotically, derive formulas for the spectral radius, and calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials for binary power graphs.

This study introduces a novel method for satellite-based localization that relies on inter-satellite ranging data. The approach involves modeling the inter-satellite distance as a function of the relative positions of the two satellites and the unknown target. By employing a least squares estimator, the target's position is derived from a set of inter-satellite distance readings. The paper analyzes the theoretical accuracy of this localization process and compares it against existing ground station and inter-satellite techniques. The findings indicate that ground station and inter-satellite methods yield comparable accuracy, yet hybridizing both yields superior results. Furthermore, the theoretical performance of the proposed inter-satellite localization is validated through simulation experiments.

Tidal interactions between a planet and its host star can alter the planet's orbit, specifically modifying its period and eccentricity. This study investigates the orbital evolution of XO-3b, a hot Jupiter with a 3.9-day period, by analyzing its orbital period decay. We introduce a new calibration framework designed for astrophysical experiments that integrates Bayesian methods with machine learning. This approach employs a hierarchical model to define the connection between calibration parameters and measurements, thereby enabling the incorporation of prior knowledge. We apply this framework to the calibration of the Hubble Space Telescope's (HST) Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3), specifically analyzing data from the Cosmic Assembly Near-IR Deep Extragalactic Survey (CANDELS). The analysis utilizes a hierarchical Gaussian process prior to model the lensing map, which is inferred from stellar images. We compare this Bayesian Gaussian process (GP) method against a traditional calibration algorithm. Results indicate that the Bayesian GP approach yields superior calibration, offering more reliable uncertainty quantification and improved generalization to unseen data.

This paper investigates central values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions arising from a cuspidal representation of GL(2) twisted by a Hecke character, alongside its twist counterpart determined by another Hecke character. We establish a lower bound for these central values applicable to a substantial set of pairs of characters, contingent upon the assumption that the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis holds true.

Conducting a clinical trial with a binary treatment and a continuous outcome is common, yet the standard approach of modeling the mean using linear regression with a log link and analyzing the resulting quantiles via quantile regression is often suboptimal. This paper introduces a new method for Constrained Longitudinal Data Analysis (CLDA) that accommodates natural cubic splines to handle continuous outcomes. This approach offers several advantages: it allows for the inclusion of a covariate, provides a more flexible fit than the traditional linear assumption, and enables the derivation of closed-form estimates for the treatment effect. These benefits are demonstrated through a simulation study and a real-world application involving a randomized trial on a binary treatment and a continuous outcome.

Crawling is a routing protocol that directs packets to their intended destinations by selecting the most suitable next hop from a set of available routes. This paper introduces CRAWLING, a routing protocol that dynamically constructs routing tables and selects next hops based on a combination of deterministic and stochastic mechanisms. Drawing inspiration from biological systems, the stochastic component incorporates a probability distribution to model routing behaviors. The protocol's performance is evaluated through extensive simulations, which demonstrate that CRAWLING surpasses existing routing protocols in terms of throughput, packet delivery ratio, and end-to-end delay.

The concept of flatness in optimization has recently gained significant attention, particularly for its ability to enhance generalization. This paper investigates the comparative dynamics of two leading flatness-based strategies for achieving scalability in flat-minima optimization: the stochastic approach and the deterministic approach. We demonstrate that these two methods are complementary rather than competing, as they excel under distinct conditions. Furthermore, we introduce a hybrid method that leverages the strengths of both stochastic and deterministic techniques to achieve superior performance. The study also reveals a critical limitation of the current deterministic approach, which is susceptible to converging toward sharp minima in high-dimensional settings. To address this, we introduce a novel deterministic technique that incorporates a specific regularization term, effectively mitigating the risk of local optima and enhancing performance in high-dimensional spaces.

This study introduces a parametric FSL capable of handling high-power signals, which relies on a nonlinear transmission line utilizing a microstrip line with integrated nonlinear inductors. The research evaluates how insertion loss and the power threshold influence performance, revealing that a lower power threshold coupled with reduced insertion loss enhances the device's ability to reduce signal attenuation. Furthermore, the FSL's performance is optimized by adjusting its physical dimensions, resulting in a setup with a power threshold of 10.16 dBm and an insertion loss of 0.01 dB.

This study examines the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak in South Korea, which experienced three distinct waves driven by the virus's spread, followed by the initial introduction and subsequent loosening of quarantine measures. We developed a model incorporating the effects of media coverage and the government's response to analyze how these factors influence the timing, duration, and intensity of each epidemic wave. Our results indicate that while media coverage significantly impacts the transmission rate, its effect on the total number of infections is limited. Furthermore, we observed that the virus's basic reproduction number declined over time, suggesting that government interventions played a crucial role in halting the expansion of each wave.

This paper presents a supervised approach to identifying terms that share semantic equivalence, such as synonyms. While prior unsupervised methods have been effective, this study introduces a machine learning framework that leverages sentence context alongside structural features derived from dependency trees to enhance matching accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that combining these graph-based structural elements with bag-of-words representations significantly boosts performance. Furthermore, we introduce a new feature that captures matching information across multiple dependency trees, which further improves results. The proposed method is evaluated on two datasets: the original English Synonymy Corpus and a new English Equivalence Corpus.

We examine a $d$-dimensional Poisson Boolean model where the probability that the origin belongs to the cluster containing it increases as $\Theta(\lambda) \sim C\lambda$ as $\lambda \to 0$, with $C$ depending on the model's parameters.

We introduce a new method for deriving barotropic and baroclinic equilibrium configurations for rapidly rotating stars, which incorporates the effects of rotation, nuclear energy generation, and radiative transfer. This approach utilizes a variational principle to minimize the total energy of a system defined by its mass distribution, composition, and velocity field. The resulting equilibrium equations are solved using a Newton-Raphson technique. Our findings demonstrate that these equilibrium states are resilient to initial conditions and exhibit stability against various internal perturbations. Furthermore, the code facilitates the investigation of stellar evolution by generating a series of connected equilibria.

This study examines the structure scalars within a generalized Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi spacetime, a model describing a general inhomogeneous and anisotropic solution to Einstein's field equations. We analyze these scalars in both weak-field and strong-field regimes, demonstrating that in the weak-field limit, they align with their counterparts in standard flat FLRW spacetime. Furthermore, we evaluate the evolution of structure scalars in the late-time era, revealing that, unlike in the standard LTB spacetime, they exhibit a non-constant behavior in the generalized framework.

In multipartite systems, strong sets are distinguished by their ability to conceal information from any single participant. Our study reveals that local hiding is achievable for tripartite systems with three or more particles, extending to scenarios involving arbitrary numbers of particles. Furthermore, we demonstrate that local hiding is impossible in bipartite systems.
